judged_text: The credential-sync feature was silently widened into always-on behavior: a proactive token refresh fetch to login.salesforce.com plus a prisma.credential.update now runs on every getConnection() for all users, even when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is false — this refresh path did not exist before the review iterations. Every self-hosted Salesforce user gets an extra outbound POST and a DB write on each connection construction (per booking/event check), and if the fetch or the new salesforceTokenSchema parse fails, calendar connections that previously worked (jsforce refreshes tokens itself) now hard-fail with a 400 HttpError.

record.issue_text: [BUG] The credential-sync feature was silently widened into always-on behavior: a proactive token refresh fetch to login.salesforce.com plus a prisma.credential.update now runs on every getConnection() for all users, even when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is false — this refresh path did not exist before the review iterations. Every self-hosted Salesforce user gets an extra outbound POST and a DB write on each connection construction (per booking/event check), and if the fetch or the new salesforceTokenSchema parse fails, calendar connections that previously worked (jsforce refreshes tokens itself) now hard-fail with a 400 HttpError.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, a new refresh flow was added that **unconditionally** POSTs to `https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token`, parses the response, and then `prisma.credential.update`s the stored key before constructing the `jsforce.Connection`. There is no guard on `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` (or any env flag) around this block, so it runs for all Salesforce users even when credential sharing is not enabled. It also introduces new hard-fail behavior (`throw new HttpError({ statusCode: 400, ... })` on non-OK `statusText`, and `parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws on schema mismatch), which can break connections that previously relied on jsforce’s own refresh behavior.
